title: GS pursues 15 trillion-won AI data center, seeks big tech leases to fund - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
content: Big tech leases seen as linchpin for financing GS's record AI data hub push The key to the 15 trillion won "Donghae artificial intelligence (AI) data center" that GS Group is pushing to complete in 2028 is whether it can secure long-term lease contracts with big tech. That is because 12 trillion won, or 80% of the total project cost, will be raised externally through project financing (PF). Because it is the largest private infrastructure project ever in Korea, spanning not only an AI data center but also traditional infrastructure, the company must prove the future business profitability to financial institutions. GS is contacting technology companies such as Amazon, Google, and MS to speed up the search for a "deep-pocketed tenant." According to the Financial Supervisory Service's electronic disclosure system on the 18th, GS Group's holding company GS Co. recently disclosed that it will inject an additional 200 billion won into its subsidiary GS AI Infra, which is leading the AI data center project, by the fourth quarter of this year. It plans to contribute 80 billion won this month first, followed by 120 billion won within the year. Including previous contributions, the holding company's total contribution will be 224 billion won. The company said the 200 billion won in capital will be used to lay the groundwork by investing in land acquisition, permits, and research services. Before full-scale construction begins, the investment will serve as a primer. After that, it plans to carry out paid-in capital increases according to the development stage. The target for equity financing is about 3 trillion won. To spread financial risk, GS established separate special-purpose companies (SPCs) for each project—"Data Center No. 1, No. 2, and No. 3"—under the newly created overarching entity GS AI Infra Co. GS Group's ultimate project goal is to build a 2.4 GW (gigawatt) AI data center. The 15 trillion won the company first presented is the "first-phase target" expense. In collaboration with GS Donghae Power and GS Engineering & Construction, it plans to complete 1.2 GW in stages in Donghae, Gangwon Province. Accordingly, the project size is expected to nearly double in the future. While "80% from others' capital" is a conventional approach, the market is focusing on the scale of this project. Among domestic conglomerates building AI data centers, the sizes ranged from several hundred billion won up to 5 trillion won, including ▲ KT's mid- to long-term project in five-year phases (5 trillion won) ▲ SK Horizon's expansion of existing centers and new construction (3 trillion won) ▲ Naver, each Sejong (650 billion won) ▲ Samsung SDS Gumi Center (427 billion won). For financial institutions to provide the massive 12 trillion won, the key is collateral in the form of big tech's long-term rent and power usage fees. The core tenant (anchor tenant) has not yet been finalized, and the company is said to be accelerating negotiations while contacting multiple global big tech firms. The company especially sees the AI data center, which intersects with related subsidiaries such as AI and construction, as a core future industry and plans to concentrate its firepower. While the goal is to complete it in 2028, the schedule could change as details are negotiated on design methods, cooling methods, and building structures. An industry official said, "Ahead of the election, the Trump administration has seen 'opposition to AI data center construction' emerge as a key issue as big tech demand has surged," and added, "Because the core competitiveness in the AI market is whether power demand can be met quickly, consistently, and stably, most of the supersized 15 trillion won project expense will likely be used to densely fill core equipment such as GPUs, transformers, and cooling facilities." title: GS builds Donghae AI data center, lifts coal plant utilization in South Korea - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
content: Local power demand from the Donghae AI campus could lift underused coal units despite policy to phase them out As GS Group released plans to build an artificial intelligence (AI) data center in Donghae, Gangwon Province, projections are emerging that, if the center goes online, the coal-fired power plant operated by GS Donghae Power nearby will see its utilization rate rise as well. For GS Group, it would be like catching two rabbits at once. According to the business community on the 18th, GS Group's holding company GS Corp. disclosed on the 14th that it plans to invest 200 billion won in GS AI Infra Corp., which is leading the Donghae AI data center project. GS Corp. plans to invest 80 billion won in September and 120 billion won in the fourth quarter of this year. GS AI Infra Corp.'s equity currently stands at 240 billion won. GS AI Infra Corp. is a company that GS Corp. established in June. In addition to GS AI Infra Corp., GS Corp. set up four entities to oversee the Donghae AI data center project: Donghae AI Campus 1, Donghae AI Campus 2, and Donghae AI Campus 3. The chief executive officer (CEO) and chief financial officer (CFO) of these entities are GS Corp. executives. GS Corp. owns 100% equity in the four newly established entities. GS Group released its plan to build the Donghae AI data center at the "National Briefing on Korea's Grand Leap: Three Mega Projects" in June. GS Group plans to build a 2.4-gigawatt (GW) AI data center on a site of about 231,000 square meters within the Bukpyeong General Industrial Complex 2 in Donghae by 2029. It plans to first build a 1.2 GW data center by 2028, then add another 1.2 GW by 2029. However, GS AI Infra Corp.'s equity stands at 240 billion won. GS Group estimates that phase one alone, a 1.2 GW data center, will cost 15 trillion won. It plans to raise 80% of the total project cost externally through project financing (PF). Through the disclosure, GS Corp. said, "For now, we plan to cover about 20% of the total investment with equity, but the equity injection ratio may change as the project proceeds." It added, "We plan to build (the data center) in phases according to contracts with customers," and "Within this year, we plan to sequentially carry out site acquisition, permits and licenses, and securing power procedures." The Bukpyeong General Industrial Complex 2, where GS Group's Donghae AI data center will be located, is an industrial complex that GS began building in 2016 and completed in 2022. The site is secured, and conditions for power supply, the core of AI data center operations, are in place. Across a two-lane road from Bukpyeong General Industrial Complex 2 is the Bukpyeong National Industrial Complex, where GS Donghae Power, a subsidiary of GS E&R, GS Group's power generation company, is located. GS Donghae Power has operated a 1.2 GW coal-fired power plant since 2018. If the Donghae AI data center goes into operation, the utilization rate of GS Donghae Power's coal-fired power plant is highly likely to rise. The plant's utilization rate currently remains around 30%. The reason is the delay in expanding the transmission network connecting the East Coast and the Seoul metropolitan area due to permitting issues for expanding the Dongseoul Substation in Hanam, Gyeonggi Province. Industry observers expect that even if the Donghae AI data center is built at 1.2 GW in phase one, the utilization rate of GS Donghae Power will rise under a "local production, local consumption (using power where it is generated)" supply model. However, GS plans to receive the power needed for the Donghae AI data center through Korea Electric Power Corporation, rather than procuring it directly from GS Donghae Power. Even if the Donghae AI data center's power demand is met through KEPCO, the increased local power demand makes it highly likely that the utilization rates of GS Donghae Power—as well as Samcheok Blue Power and Gangneung Eco Power, whose utilization has been low due to a shortage of transmission lines—will rise. A power industry official said, "Because the grid is interconnected, it becomes hard to say the Donghae AI data center uses only the power coming from GS Donghae Power's coal-fired plant," adding, "For GS Group, it's a structure that allows it to run the data center and also capture power supply gains." However, if GS Donghae Power's utilization rate rises, criticism may emerge that this runs counter to the government's policy direction of early retirement for coal-fired power plants. The government on this day released detailed plans to retire coal-fired power plants in 2040, but expansion of AI data centers could instead increase the use of coal-fired power plants. Of the 60 coal-fired power units currently in operation, the government decided to replace 39 units, whose 30-year design life ends by 2040, with liquefied natural gas (LNG) plants or pumped-storage plants by 2038. Instead, most of the 21 units subject to early retirement that still have remaining design life after 2040 will be sequentially retired between 2037 and 2039, with up to 10 designated as "security power sources" and kept for a few more years. GS Donghae Power's design life runs until 2047, making it one of the 21 units subject to early retirement. A GS official said, "It's true we are in contact with many companies, including big tech," but added, "No one has yet signed a data center use contract." The official added, "The market believes construction will start in Nov., but due to permitting issues, it could be later than known." We use cookies to enhance your experience and analyze traffic.
